contamination.description: Share of the rows the forest ranks as most anomalous. It flags exactly this share of whatever it is given, so the count is only a ranking; whether any row stands out is `alpha` and `min_excess`.

alpha.description: Chance that jointly normal data has a row called far, over all its rows. A row is far when its robust Mahalanobis distance is beyond the chi-squared point that leaves `alpha / rows` above it.

min_rows_per_column.description: Rows per column below which no row is called far: the spread of so few rows is too loose a ruler.

min_excess.description: How far the forest's top anomaly score must be above the top score it gives a normal sample of the same shape for a row to stand out. Scores vary by 0.01 to 0.02 between samples of that shape, and a median standing in for missing values lifts them by 0.02.

min_n.description: Finite values a column needs to be a feature.

max_missing_share.description: Share of missing values above which a column is not a feature. A missing value takes the column's median, so a column that is mostly missing makes the rows that have a value look far from the rest.

max_rows.description: Most rows fitted; a larger frame is sampled with `seed`.

seed.description: Seed of the forest and of the sample.

n_flagged.description: Rows the forest ranks as most anomalous (`contamination`).

far_rows.description: Rows whose robust Mahalanobis distance is beyond the limit, so far from the rest of the cloud together; 0 too when there are too few rows per column to say.

far_limit.description: That limit, a squared distance; None when it was not applied.

example_rows.description: Positions in the data of the rows that stand out most: the far rows, then the forest's ranking.

max_anomaly_score.description: Highest anomaly score, from 0 to 1; near 0.5 for all rows when none stands out, and approaching 1 for a clear anomaly.

reference_max_score.description: The highest score the same forest gives a normal sample of the same rows and columns: what chance alone reaches.
